title: Nuh 71:21-24 with words spaced, and the questions
subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
source: Written for quran/y8 lesson 41 (Pupil PDF worksheet: Nuh 71:21-24 with words spaced, and the questions)
intro: Lesson 41. Read each word slowly, pointing with your finger. Only the Arabic is the Qur'an; the English is a translation of its meaning.

arabic.text: قَالَ نُوحٌۭ رَّبِّ إِنَّهُمْ عَصَوْنِى وَٱتَّبَعُوا۟ مَن لَّمْ يَزِدْهُ مَالُهُۥ وَوَلَدُهُۥٓ إِلَّا خَسَارًۭا (٢١) وَمَكَرُوا۟ مَكْرًۭا كُبَّارًۭا (٢٢) وَقَالُوا۟ لَا تَذَرُنَّ ءَالِهَتَكُمْ وَلَا تَذَرُنَّ وَدًّۭا وَلَا سُوَاعًۭا وَلَا يَغُوثَ وَيَعُوقَ وَنَسْرًۭا (٢٣) وَقَدْ أَضَلُّوا۟ كَثِيرًۭا ۖ وَلَا تَزِدِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ إِلَّا ضَلَٰلًۭا (٢٤)

head: Ayah
Translation of the meaning (Saheeh International)
rows: Noah said, "My Lord, indeed they have disobeyed me and followed him whose wealth and children will not increase him except in loss.
And they conspired an immense conspiracy.
And said, 'Never leave your gods and never leave Wadd or Suwa' or Yaghuth and Ya'uq and Nasr.
And already they have misled many. And, [my Lord], do not increase the wrongdoers except in error."

head: Word
Where
Rule
How to read it
rows: Idgham without ghunnah: tanween into ر
Idgham without ghunnah: noon into ل

questions.q: Chunk and link Nuh 71:21-24 together, ayah by ayah.
questions.a: The class recites 71:21-24 together without the mushaf.

questions.q: Listening rota: today's group recites 71:21-24 to the teacher, one by one. Everyone else: 3-3-link the same ayat, then tick the revision log.
questions.a: Pupil recites with no help; the teacher marks hifdh and tajweed on the rubric and gives one target.
A tremendous plot against the truth.

questions.q: Why is idgham into ل and ر without ghunnah?
questions.a: These two letters are very close in makhraj; the noon merges fully and its ghunnah disappears.

questions.q: What did the leaders tell the people (71:23)?
questions.a: A) Do not leave your gods. 71:23.

questions.q: Nuh 71:23: «وَقَالُوا۟ لَا ...» Which word comes next?
Think again: Nuh's people followed leaders whose wealth and children only increased them in loss (71:21). Why do people follow the rich and famous even when they are wrong?
questions.a: Status and fear of being different; the Qur'an teaches us to follow truth, not popularity.
